title: Lifting one finite separable residue extension
statement: Let R be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with residue field kappa, and let L be a finite separable field extension of kappa [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. There exists a finite etale R-algebra S [def-weil-etale-morphism] and a kappa-algebra isomorphism $\kappa\otimes_R S\cong L$.

proof.text: For a local finite etale R-algebra A, its maximal ideal n contracts to m by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical]. Since localization of A at n is A itself, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal] gives mA = n. Thus its reduction is its residue field. This observation applies to the finite local factor selected in the next step; no preliminary decomposition of arbitrary finite etale algebras is needed.

source.place: Tag 04GK, using Tag 00U4 for a finite local etale factor

proof.text: (Lifting one finite separable extension.) Let $\kappa'/\kappa$ be a finite separable field extension. Since $R$ is local, $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=R_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak mR_{\mathfrak m}=R/\mathfrak m=\kappa$. By Stacks 00UD [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-prescribed-residue-field] there are $R\to S$ with $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ etale, a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ over $\mathfrak m$ and a $\kappa$-isomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\kappa'$. $S$ is of finite type over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] (1), so by Stacks 04GJ [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-type-product-decomposition] $S\cong A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\times B$ with $A_i$ local and finite over $R$ and $R\to B$ not quasi-finite at any prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak m$. Each factor is a localization of $S$ at an idempotent, hence etale over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] (2); in particular $R\to B$ is quasi-finite at every prime of $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-quasi-finite] ('since $R\to S$ is quasi-finite'), so $B$ has no prime over $\mathfrak m$. The primes of a finite product are those of the factors, so $\mathfrak q$ comes from a prime of some $A_i$ over $\mathfrak m$, which by the preceding local-factor observation is its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_i=\mathfrak mA_i$; thus $S_{\mathfrak q}=A_i$. So $A_i$ is a finite etale $R$-algebra with $F(A_i)=A_i/\mathfrak mA_i=\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\kappa'$ as $\kappa$-algebras.
